entries.alt: The Domains screen: Quick add and Guided add buttons, a search field, and the table of example.com, example.net and example.org with their aliases, status, connections and row actions.

The configuration pages of example.org (Overview, Connections and discovery, Sign-in policy, Domain aliases, Login hostnames, Diagnostics) above the overview counts of backends, aliases, login hosts and sign-in rules.

The Service backends list of example.org: the failover checkbox turned on, and three backends, imap-primary, imap-standby and smtp, with protocol, host and port, priority and status; imap-primary and smtp are marked Selected.

The backend editor for imap-primary: Service and selection with ID, protocol, priority, Enabled and Preferred, then the Connection fields host, port, connection security and private-network permission.
The Allowlist field containing *@example.org and the Blocklist field containing former.*@example.org.
The Apply domain changes? dialog listing the Sign-in blocklist before and after the change, with Cancel and Apply changes buttons.
The Domain aliases page of example.org with the alias corp.example.org and the Add alias button.
The Login host mappings page of example.org with the host webmail.example.org and a field to add another.
The Connection and DNS checks card with the buttons Test saved connections and Check DNS.
The Add a domain with guidance wizard on its first step, Domain identity, with corp.example.com entered as the domain name.
The Connection step of the wizard with Configure a mail server chosen: IMAP on imap.example.com port 993 with TLS from connection start, and an outgoing SMTP server smtp.example.com on port 465.
The Review step of the wizard listing the domain corp.example.com, the IMAP and SMTP servers and the connection policy, with the Create domain button.
The Edit backend screen for the backend exchange of example.net, with EWS chosen as the protocol, priority 100, and Enabled and Preferred for this service checked.

The backend editor for the EWS backend exchange of example.net: the Exchange Web Services endpoint, EWS authentication set to NTLMv2 with the Windows domain EXAMPLE, and the optional CA certificates field.
The Sign-in policy tab of the Security centre: the introduction and the start of the First sign-in rule by type table.
The First sign-in rule by type table: New users set to Open and the password, single sign-on and linked mailbox rows set to Inherit.
The Pre-added users card: the address list, note and lifetime fields, the Add pending users button, and two pending entries for jordan.ellis@example.com and lena.brooks@example.com.
The Would a new sign-in be refused? check: an address field, the sign-in type and the Check button.
The user alex@example.com on the Users screen with the Access and removal tab open, showing the Mailwoman access card.
The Mailwoman access card on the Access and removal tab of alex@example.com, with the Block login and Delete local access buttons.
The Block Mailwoman login confirmation for alex@example.com, explaining that blocking revokes current sessions and does not change the upstream mailbox.

The Aggregate and adaptive protection tab of the Security centre: a notice that country features have no country database, the seven sub-tabs, and the Current policy card showing request budgets and adaptive protection both off.
The request protection sub-tabs Overview, Aggregate, Adaptive, Protocol guard, Probing, Object state and Decisions, numbered 1 to 7.
The What happens today card: request budget off, recognized scan paths enforced, unusual request protection off, and the slow-down, block and clean-record durations.
The Presets card with the choices Relaxed, Balanced and Strict.
The Request budget group on the Aggregate sub-tab: the Request budget switch set to Off, the requests per address, per mailbox and per administrator, and the budget window, numbered 1 to 5.
The Recognized scan paths rule on the Adaptive sub-tab, with its setting key security.protection.probePathMode, its explanation and the value Enforce.
The What happens group on the Adaptive sub-tab: Slow-down 3 seconds, Block 5 minutes and Clean record after 1 day.
The Probing protection card: its explanation, the warning that a block also refuses the mail app from that address, and the Off and On buttons with On selected.
The Overall mode card of the Protocol guard sub-tab: the Off, Detect and Enforce buttons, the current state Mixed, and the count of requests that enforcing would refuse (masked).
The Framing and smuggling group of the Protocol guard sub-tab, with the request framing and body framing classes and their modes.
The first rules of the Browsers and crawlers group: User-Agent protection set to Enforce, Block recognized bots on the first request switched on, and the categories to count.
The first two rules of the Detection and evidence group on the Probing sub-tab: the four counted misses, all selected, and the Probe paths list beginning with /+cscoe+, /.aws and /.env.
The Audit and logging group of the Probing sub-tab: the source address in the audit log set to masked and the fail2ban log line on block switched on.
The SSH tunnels tab of Integrations with no tunnels configured, and the New SSH tunnel and Refresh buttons.
A new SSH tunnel form with the SSH server identity section: tunnel name, SSH server hostname, port and login username.
The DANE verification, MTA-STS verification and SMTP policy domain fields of an SMTP connection, with MTA-STS set to Follow the published policy and example.org as the policy domain.
The LDAP / GAL directory tab of Integrations with one new directory being filled in: server URL, search base, service bind DN, transport security and connection policy.

One directory entry: server URL, search base, bind DN, transport security, priority, connection policy, the two checkboxes, the stored-password action with a new password field, and the five attribute fields.
The Single sign-on page with two OpenID Connect providers: Staff sign-in for the whole deployment, enabled, and Partner sign-in for example.org, disabled.
The editor of the Staff sign-in provider: backend ID, display name, protocol OIDC, scope, first-login policy and the OpenID Connect fields.
The Claim mapping group: email, username, display-name and groups claim fields.

The SAML part of a new provider: provider metadata upload, IdP SSO and logout URLs, signing certificates, and this server's entity ID, ACS URL, NameID format and the signed and encrypted assertion switches.
The OAuth clients page with self-registration off, no allowed redirect host, and the shared registration token not required.
The What a registered app gets group: the Read, Send and Delete permissions, the Mail and Calendar, contacts, tasks and notes parts of the account, and the requests-per-minute limit.
The Identity provider page with the issuer enabled at https://mail.example.com/oidc and two identity clients, Team wiki and Room booking desktop app.
The Client access tab with both controls off: Require a private client address with its address segment, Require a pre-shared key with a new key field, and the grant lifetime of 24 hours.
The editor of the identity client Room booking desktop app: public client authentication, a loopback callback URI and the allowed identity scopes.
The issuer form of the identity provider with the public HTTPS issuer URL and the signing key rotation.
The Security centre on its Client access tab, below the notice that country features are on without a country database, with both entry controls off.
The Protocol guard sub-tab of Aggregate and adaptive protection, with its explanation and the Overall mode card.

The Overview tab of the Security centre: the row of tabs, a warning that country features are on without a country database, and tiles for two-factor adoption, failed sign-ins, request protection, sign-in locks, probing blocks, admin sessions and security posture.
The Two-factor & sign-in requirements tab: the Require two-factor for the whole deployment checkbox, a per-domain table for example.com and example.org, and the list of passkey and session policies.
The Security policy tab of the Security centre: the Connections group with the lowest TLS version, the start of the Sign-in group, and the Save bar.
The Sign-in group of the Security policy: Require a second factor for every account, Argon2 memory, Argon2 passes and Argon2 parallelism.
The Reading group of the Security policy: the Reading floor and Screen capture protection fields.

The Personal security tab of My preferences: Administrator passkeys with a name field and Add administrator passkey, the Authenticator app section with Manage authenticator and recovery codes, and the Change your password form.
The Confirm it is you dialog over the authenticator page, asking for the administrator's password before setup starts.
Authenticator setup in progress: the QR code and the manual setup key (both hidden here), the Authenticator code field and the Confirm authenticator button.
The Sessions tab: domain, account ID and client type filters, Preview session revocation, and a table with Alex Rivera's mailbox session (times hidden) and its Revoke session button.
The Temporary sign-in locks tab with no locks: Configure sign-in limits, the Sign-in surface filter, the search field and Refresh locks.

The Sign-in country policy diagnostic with no country database: the warning that active policies refuse sign-in, the configure buttons, and the table of the trusted source IP, resolved country, database state, scope and both sign-in decisions.
The IP ban list with two bans, 203.0.113.45 active until removed and 198.51.100.23 with an expiry date, each with its reason and an Unban button.

fill.label: @admin-obs-ban-reason
fill.value: Credential stuffing seen in the sign-in log

entries.alt: The ban editor with the address 192.0.2.77 and a reason filled in, an empty expiry field and the Save IP ban button.
The Admin console and API card of Inbound access, not yet restricted, with two rescue entries typed in (192.0.2.10/32 and 2001:db8:10::/48) and an empty hostnames list.

The Deployment checks tab: Find a check, the Status filter, and the start of the table with HTTP admission and request limits, inbound connection negotiation limits and the HTTPS request check marked Review needed.

The deployment checks filtered to Review needed on the plain-HTTP demo server: HTTPS request, Secure cookies, Enabled administrators without a second factor and Encryption at rest, with their observed values.
The IP ban list tab of the Security centre, below the country database warning: the explanation of what a ban does, Add ban, the search field and two bans.
The Temporary sign-in locks tab of the Security centre with no active locks.
The Sign-in country policy tab of the Security centre on a server without a country database.
The Inbound access tab of the Security centre: Refresh saved policy and DNS status and the start of the Admin console and API card.
The Sessions tab of the Security centre with its filters and the session revocation controls.
My preferences open on the Personal security tab, with Administrator passkeys and the Authenticator app section.
The admin console sign-in form with the Admin username and Password fields and the Sign in button, markers 1 and 2 on the two fields.

The admin console on the Dashboard: the navigation grouped under My account, Overview, People, Security and Configuration on the left, the search button at the top right, and the setup checklist, account counts and request history in the main column.
The console navigation with markers 1 to 6 on its groups: My account, Overview, People, Security, Configuration and Operations, each listing its sections.
The dashboard setup checklist with one item done and two open, each with an Open link and a Hide button; markers on a Done status, an Open link and a Hide button.
The console search window with domain typed, listing matching sections, domains and settings.
The session bar at the bottom of the console: Signed in as admin and the idle timeout countdown.
entries.note: The countdown is computed from the server clock, so its seconds can differ by one or two between runs.
